tasks.title: Reachability primitive: check_wired over the import graph
acceptance_criteria: harness/wire_up.py exposes WireResult, LIVE_ROOTS, and check_wired
check_wired returns wired=False for a module no live root reaches, wired=True for a module a live root reaches
tasks.objective: Create the new, pure, stdlib-only module harness/wire_up.py that decides whether a module is WIRED (reachable from a live entrypoint) by reusing harness.rebuild.discover, with no process/network/agent calls.

spec.objective: Create the new, pure, stdlib-only module harness/wire_up.py that decides whether a module is WIRED (reachable from a live entrypoint) by reusing harness.rebuild.discover, with no process/network/agent calls.
functional_requirements: Expose a dataclass WireResult with fields wired: bool, importers: list[str], reason: str, fix_hint: str.

Expose a module-level constant LIVE_ROOTS: a list of the repository's real live entrypoint module rel-paths, including (at least) orchestrator, orchestrator_worker, autowork_daemon, the planner cli, the claude/gemini hook entrypoints, webui_control, and the overseer/services entrypoints. Use the rel-paths as discover.discover_modules reports them (POSIX, e.g. 'harness/orchestrator.py').
Expose check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots=LIVE_ROOTS, exclude=()) -> WireResult.

Build the intra-project import graph by calling harness.rebuild.discover.discover_modules(repo_root) to get the non-test module list and harness.rebuild.discover.module_import_graph(repo_root, modules) to get {module_rel -> set(modules it imports)}. Do NOT re-parse imports yourself.

Decide WIRED by a breadth-first traversal seeded from the modules in `roots` that exist in the graph: a module is reachable if it is imported (directly or transitively) by some root. new_module_rel is WIRED iff it is in the reachable set AND at least one of its direct importers (excluding any path in `exclude`) is itself reachable from a root.
Report the reachable direct importers of new_module_rel (minus `exclude`) in WireResult.importers.
Hard-fail (wired=False) with an actionable reason+fix_hint when no live importer reaches the module (the orphan case).

Supplement: before declaring orphan, grep the repo's config/** files for the module's stem/symbol; if referenced there (dynamic/config-string wiring), treat as wired with a reason noting the config reference.
spec.interfaces: WireResult(wired: bool, importers: list[str], reason: str, fix_hint: str); LIVE_ROOTS: list[str]; check_wired(repo_root, new_module_rel, *, roots=LIVE_ROOTS, exclude=()) -> WireResult. Consumes harness.rebuild.discover.discover_modules(source_root) -> (modules, tests, seeds) and harness.rebuild.discover.module_import_graph(source_root, modules) -> dict[str, set[str]] unchanged.
edge_cases: A module imported ONLY by another orphan (inbound-degree > 0 but not reachable from any root) must be wired=False -- traverse from roots, never trust mere inbound degree.
A module imported only by its own oracle/test must be wired=False; the exclude= argument lets the caller drop the module's own oracle so it cannot launder itself.
A live root itself is not flagged as orphan: seed the BFS from roots, do not require roots to have inbound importers.
A new_module_rel not present in the discovered module set returns wired=False with a clear reason rather than raising.
non_goals: No integration into the orchestrator accept path, the overseer gates, or the plan validator -- those are separate leaves; this leaf is the pure primitive only.
No process spawn, model/API/network call, or un-injected subprocess; only stdlib + discover + filesystem reads.
spec.implementation_notes: EMIT harness/wire_up.py AS A SINGLE WHOLE NEW FILE (this is a brand-new module -- produce the entire file contents, not a patch/diff). Pure stdlib only: dataclasses, collections (deque/defaultdict), pathlib, os, re for the config grep. Import discover_modules and module_import_graph from harness.rebuild.discover. Algorithm: modules,_,_ = discover_modules(Path(repo_root)); graph = module_import_graph(Path(repo_root), modules) is {mod -> set(mods it imports)}. To find what reaches new_module_rel, build the REVERSE: importers[d] gathers every m whose graph[m] contains d. Compute the reachable set by BFS from the roots present in `modules`, following forward edges (graph[m]) so reachable = everything a root can import transitively. new_module_rel is WIRED iff some module in (importers[new_module_rel] - set(exclude)) is in the reachable set. importers list in WireResult = sorted(that intersection). If empty, run the config grep: scan files under repo_root/config (recursively) for the module's stem (new_module_rel without dir/.py) as a whole word; if found, return wired=True reason='referenced in config (dynamic wiring)'. Otherwise wired=False, reason names the orphan, fix_hint suggests adding an import/call from a live module. Keep LIVE_ROOTS accurate to THIS repo's layout (harness/orchestrator.py, harness/orchestrator_worker.py, harness/autowork_daemon.py, harness/planner/cli.py, and the hook + webui + overseer/service entrypoints as they appear in discover's output). Do NOT cite line numbers. The committed oracle below is authoritative -- your code MUST make it pass.

unit_tests: module reachable from a root is wired
regression_tests: imported-only-by-orphan is still unwired (BFS-from-roots, not inbound degree)
test_spec.test_data_requirements: A synthetic source tree written under tmp_path with root.py importing wired_mod, plus orphan_mod, chain_mod, and a selftest pair -- supplied by the committed oracle.
